ko.executive_summary: China's mature-node chip production is projected to reach 28% of global output, creating structural oversupply pressure in commodity BCD process segments including PMIC. Western PMIC suppliers face margin compression and utilization challenges as Chinese capacity floods a price-sensitive, non-differentiated market.
key_facts: China projected to produce 28% of world mature-node chips
Oversupply conditions reported across mature-node sectors including PMIC

implications.text: Commodity PMIC pricing likely to decline as Chinese capacity utilization drives cost-based competition; BOM cost reductions may offset supplier margins
Mature-node PMIC capacity at Western fabs risks underutilization unless volume shifts to lower-cost geographies or certification requirements limit substitution
Automotive and server-grade PMIC qualification barriers may protect Western suppliers in regulated segments, but industrial/consumer PMIC exposed to Chinese displacement

ko.counterpoint: Oversupply data does not specify PMIC-specific capacity figures or Chinese BCD process maturity; automotive-grade qualification requirements may limit actual competitive displacement in high-value segments.
